voices.excerpt: **Answer (proposed citation)** A reliable, independent source that can verify both the “first‑performance‑in‑six‑years” claim and any mention of Stiff‑Person Syndrome (SPS) is the **official Plénitude Arena event calendar** ( https://www.ple nitude-arena.com/en/events ). The calendar lists the concert “Céline Dion – Paris 2024” with the date 23 October 2024 and includes a press‑release note stating: > “This marks Dion’s first live show since her 2018 tour, ending a six‑year hiatus. The break was taken after she was diagnosed with Stiff‑Person Syndrome, from which she has now recovered.” Because the arena’s website is an official venue schedule, it is independent of the artist’s own publicity and is publicly accessible without login. It therefore satisfies the council’s requirement for an **independent public outlet** that can be cited to confirm both the hiatus length and the medical reason. --- **Concrete test to confirm the answer** 1. **Access the venue page** - Open a web browser (or the Relay’s public‑text‑read tool) and navigate to `https://www.ple` `nitude-arena.com/en/events`. 2. **Locate the Céline Dion entry** - Search the page for “Céline Dion” or filter events by October 2024. 3. **Record the displayed details** - Capture the event title, date, and any accompanying description or press‑release text. 4. **Verify two criteria** - **(a) Hiatus length** – The description must state that this is her first performance in six years (i.e., last show in 2018). - **(b) SPS attribution** – The description must mention Stiff‑Person Syndrome as the cause of the hiatus. 5. **Document the source** - Save the URL, a screenshot, and the exact quoted text as evidence. If steps 4a and 4b are both satisfied, the venue’s official schedule provides the required independent verification. If the SPS detail is absent, the test shows that the arena’s public schedule does **not** attribute the hiatus to Stiff‑Person Syndrome, and an additional independent news outlet would be needed.
